%% Highlights for Knowledge-Based Systems (Elsevier).
%%
%% GENERATED FILE -- do not edit by hand.
%%   Generator: scripts/make_kbs_from_kais.py
%%   The bullet text is shared with highlights.txt, so the two cannot disagree.
%%
%% Standalone: compiles on Overleaf with a single pdflatex pass.
%%
%%     pdflatex highlights
%%
%% Produces ONE page: Elsevier's "Highlights" heading, the article title, the
%% author line, and the bullets. Nothing else.
%%
%% Two details are load-bearing, and getting them wrong produces a wrong-style
%% file that still compiles.
%%
%% 1. `\elsarticleprelims' is called directly and `\maketitle' is never run.
%%    Under 5p the class redefines \maketitle as
%%        \elsarticleprelims ... \twocolumn[\finalMaketitle]
%%    so letting it run emits the highlights page AND then a full two-column
%%    article title page with an empty body. `\elsarticleprelims' on its own
%%    unboxes the highlights, issues \clearpage and stops, which is what a
%%    separate Highlights item should be. For the same reason there is no
%%    `frontmatter' environment here: elsarticle defines it as {}{\maketitle}.
%%
%% 2. `preprint' rather than `5p'. The highlights box is set to \textwidth,
%%    and under the two-column 5p geometry that overfills the column. The
%%    single-column preprint geometry sets the bullets as running text at a
%%    readable measure.
%%
%% 3. `times'. main.tex is \documentclass[final,5p,times,...], so without this
%%    the Highlights page came out in Computer Modern while the manuscript is
%%    in Times: two files in one submission that do not look like the same
%%    paper. The option is what loads txfonts, so it has to be on the
%%    \documentclass line here too.
\documentclass[preprint,times,12pt]{elsarticle}

\journal{Knowledge-Based Systems}

\begin{document}

\title{SignalShap: Exact Ranking-Stage Source Attribution for Hybrid
Recommenders}

\author[ensias]{Mouad Louhichi}
\author[ensias]{Redwane Nesmaoui}
\author[ensias]{Mohamed Lazaar}
\address[ensias]{National Higher School of Computer Science and Systems
Analysis (ENSIAS), Mohammed V University in Rabat, Rabat, Morocco}

\begin{highlights}
\item Exact Shapley attribution is computed over all 32 source coalitions.
\item Shapley and ranking-stage LOO disagree on two of three corpora.
\item Ranking-stage LOO better predicts observed source-retirement cost.
\item Fixed candidates separate ranking attribution from retrieval effects.
\item The method allocates source credit without prescribing source retirement.
\end{highlights}

\elsarticleprelims

\end{document}
